title: After Midnight
dateline: Selrick Academy, the night of Fanny’s first day.
mood: Second place for the first time. Layla works in secret through the night, then races Fanny for drones.

hero.alt: Layla aims her long white cannon down a white corridor, a counter glowing by her head.

segs.t: Layla heard every word through the closing doors. She did not turn around.
Her lab was an abandoned classroom she had taken against the rules. Three black drones rose to meet her, each with an angry face she had drawn on in cyan marker.
A message from home: “Second is still wonderful, darling! You’re the hope of this family.” Her family had been scientists for generations. She left it unanswered.
Behind spare capacitors on the top shelf stood her gold FIRST PLACE trophy. She turned it to face the wall.

Then she worked on the cannon she had built. Low charge shot true. Full charge pulled left, a hand’s width at two hundred meters. She had rebuilt barrel and sight twice. The fault was somewhere in how the power came up.
ERROR, said the console in red: one more line in a log that went back months.

media.alt: Layla types at her lab console while her drones hover, until the screens flash red with warnings and a drone glares at the camera.

segs.t: Last, she checked the seedling under its glass dome, the only thing there she had not built.
After midnight she slipped into the VR Battlefield and signed the night log. Her name filled the page, at lunch hours and late nights, back to her first year.
Beside every line someone had made a small stylus tick, the same slant each time.
The system ticks everything,
she assumed. She had never checked.
At home, talent had been enough. At the Academy the courses got hard. So she trained in secret, and told everyone the exams were easy.

media.alt: Fanny and Layla glare past a nervous boy, under boxes saying Layla acts as if she does not care, though it leaves her bitter.

segs.t: She ran Fanny’s assessment five times, leaving the simulated man under his sign. Her best was 3:40. Fanny’s record read 3:39, CIVILIAN RECOVERED, +0:11.
Without him, she did it in 3:28,
Layla thought. At two in the morning, she gave up.
Three mornings running, at a quarter past five, Layla lay on the dark gallery above the drill hall. Her drone filmed Fanny.
Fanny drilled alone in the hall’s one narrow doorway, blades out. Anything that came at her there had to take turns.
That’s the alley thing?
It was so simple it made her angry.
On the third morning, Fanny turned toward the gallery. Layla pressed her face to the floor. The drone did not. It rose over the rail to keep Fanny in frame.
“Who’s there?! Phew, you startled me.” Fanny laughed and told the drone kindly that it must be lost.
Layla called it home with two taps.
In training, she needled Fanny at every turn. She made everything a race, too.
“Careful,” she said on the climbing wall. “Someone up there might need carrying.”
“I’ll look,” said Fanny. She reached the top first, found nobody, and reported it. She did not seem to know it had been a race.
On the fourth day they reached the drill hall door together. Layla made sure she went through first. Fanny caught up. “Layla! Let’s train together.”
Layla gave her the smile she kept for teachers. “Train together? Sorry, let’s do it another time.”

At the week’s end came a test match in the white training corridor. It was long and narrow, with lockers down both walls and a dark doorway at the far end. Out of that doorway came the practice drones: round and blue, with a glowing arrow for a face. They flew at you and burst when hit.

Over each girl’s head floated a counter of the drones she had destroyed. The swarm was shared. Every drone Fanny took was one Layla could not. Weapons were set to training power, enough to burst a drone and bruise a girl.
At the start line Layla stood half a step ahead. Fanny stepped level without noticing. Layla moved up again.
“I’m ready. The test is about to start.”
“It’s just a test match! There’s no way I’d be nervous.”
“I didn’t ask,” said Fanny.

The drones came in waves, and Fanny met them in the air. Flying was banned on school grounds, except in this hall. She wore her suit: white armor, and at her hips a rig of two long cases like folded wings. Each case held a blade. Thrusters in them lifted her.
Her blades lit cyan, and every drone they touched burst. By the last wave her counter read 0150. Then 0151.

media.alt: Fanny smiles over her glowing blade in a white corridor while the counter by her head ticks from 0150 to 0151.

segs.t: She shot down the corridor upside down. Two thin shining cables ran from her rig to the ceiling and pulled her up. Then she spun in the air, both blades out, and the drones around her burst.

media.alt: Fanny darts off and flies the white corridor upside down, then two thin cables pull her up and she spins with both blades out.

segs.t: Layla’s counter read 0148. She shot the next drone through the middle: 0149. Two behind. She narrowed her eyes at Fanny’s number and did the sum.

media.alt: A big counter reads 0148, then 0149, as small drones fly down the corridor, then Layla narrows her eyes.

segs.t: The drones came out of the far doorway one behind another. A narrow place, one line: the alley thing, turned around. One full charge down that line would take the whole row.
Fanny stood just left of that line.
Room enough,
thought Layla.
She swung the cannon up. It was as tall as she was, white with a teal strip. The cyan cells on its stock filled one by one, and lightning crawled around the muzzle.

media.alt: Layla swings her long white cannon up and charges it until a ball of light and lightning bursts from the muzzle.

segs.t: “You can’t escape my magic gun!”
The shot pulled left. It passed Fanny’s shoulder by a hand’s width and caught only one drone at the edge of the row. 0150. The rest flew on.
Fanny laughed. “That’s the alley thing! So you did hear me!”
“Hear what?”
Fanny launched at the row herself. Her rig spread open. She spun through the drones, and they burst around her in orange sparks.

media.alt: Fanny stands in the corridor with her blades low, then takes off with her rig spread like wings and spins through a burst of orange sparks.

segs.t: She rose to the ceiling. The drones that climbed after her met her blades.

media.alt: Fanny rises to the ceiling and cuts the small blue drones that fly up at her.

segs.t: Layla aimed again, low charge this time. Then she ran along the lockers and spun as the drones flew past.

media.alt: Layla runs sideways along the corridor with her cannon raised and spins as drones fly past her.

segs.t: From the ceiling Fanny swept down to the floor. She cut two drones on the way and a big one at the bottom. 0157.

media.alt: In a wide shot Fanny drops from the ceiling down the corridor, cutting drones, and slashes a big one as her counter reaches 0157.

segs.t: Layla tossed her cannon up, caught it one-handed and planted it with a crack of light.
If I can’t win the count, I’ll win the look.

media.alt: Seen from behind, Layla tosses her cannon into the air, catches it with one hand and plants it in a flash of light.

segs.t: She walked to the middle of the corridor, one fist tight at her chest. Then she lifted the cannon over her head and brought it down level across her body.

media.alt: Layla walks to the middle of the corridor, clenches a fist at her chest, then lifts her cannon overhead and brings it down level.

segs.t: The swarm ran out. Fanny’s counter stopped at 0157. Layla’s stopped at 0151.
Fanny landed beside her, pink in the face and grinning. “Training is fun.”
Layla walked out first, before her hands could shake. In the empty corridor they shook anyway. She gripped the strap in both fists and waited.

It took a long time. When she passed the window at the corridor’s end, Fanny was already out on the grass behind the hall. She lay alone in the sun as if no counter had ever existed. Birds crossed over her.
Fanny opened her eyes and reached one hand up at the sky, fingers spread.

media.alt: Seen from far above, Fanny lies alone in a sunny green field as birds fly over, then, close up, she opens her eyes and reaches a hand toward the sky.

segs.t: “I’m going to take back first place!”
